title: Understand Sort Phase Transitions: Preload → Day Sort → Twilight (and Why They Must Cycle)
summary: Use the documented rationale for sorter sort-phase transitions (preload, day sort, twilight) to interpret why the system cycles between phases and why it cannot run one sort phase continuously into the next without clearing/pushing out volume.
when_to_use: When you need to interpret observed sorter behavior that appears to be transitioning between sort phases (preload → day sort → twilight), especially when volume/destination characteristics change and you want to understand why the system must cycle rather than run one phase into another.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Identify which sort phase is currently in effect conceptually (preload, day sort, twilight) and use the documented transition rationale to explain/justify why transitions occur.
access_or_tools_needed: Operational awareness of sorter sort phases (preload/day sort/twilight) as described in the provided training video segment.

visual_references.description: Training video frame (segment 0019) containing the explanation that sorts (preload/day sort/twilight) must be cycled and cannot run into each other because volume goes to different locations; transitions still occur even in peak season.

steps.title: Identify the current sort phase conceptually (preload, day sort, twilight)
steps.purpose: So you can interpret subsequent transitions using the correct phase-to-phase rationale.
steps.instruction: From the documented set of sort phases, determine whether the system is in the conceptual phase of preload, day sort, or twilight.
steps.expected_result: You can name the active conceptual phase as one of: preload, day sort, or twilight.
steps.healthy_condition: Your phase identification matches the operational context you are observing (i.e., you can consistently map what you see to one of the three named phases).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot confidently map the observed behavior to preload vs day sort vs twilight, or you mix phases when explaining transitions.

actions.label: Select the conceptual phase
actions.exact_action: Identify which sort phase you are in conceptually from the documented set: preload, day sort, and twilight.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Sort phases (preload, day sort, twilight) must be cycled; they can’t run into each other because volume goes to different locations; even in peak season, transitions still occur.

steps.title: Confirm the operational requirement that sort phases must be cycled (not run into each other)
steps.purpose: To ensure you interpret transitions as expected behavior driven by the system’s phase design constraints.
steps.instruction: Use the documented requirement that preload/day sort/twilight must be cycled in and cannot run into each other.
steps.expected_result: You can state that the system cycles between sort phases and does not run one phase continuously into the next without clearing.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation aligns with the documented rule: phases must be cycled in because volume goes to different locations.
steps.failure_condition: You assume the system should be able to run one sort phase directly into another without transitions/clearing.

actions.label: Validate the cycling rule
actions.exact_action: Confirm the documented operational requirement: sorts must be cycled in (they do not run into each other).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: You have sorts such as preload, day sort, and twilight... all these sorts have to be cycled in... they can't just run into each other because the volume is going to different locations... even in peak season, you still have those transitions.

steps.title: Interpret transitions using the documented reason: different volume/destinations require pushing out volume before the phase ends
steps.purpose: To explain why transitions occur during normal operation and what “normal” looks like conceptually.
steps.instruction: Use the documented rationale: during each sort phase you expect to receive different volume destined for different locations, and the operational goal is to push out that volume before the sort ends—therefore the next phase requires cycling rather than continuous operation.
steps.expected_result: You can justify an observed transition by explaining that the incoming volume/destination characteristics change by phase, so the system must push out the current phase’s volume before moving on.
steps.healthy_condition: Your interpretation matches the documented cause: volume goes to different locations across phases, so phases must cycle.
steps.failure_condition: You interpret a transition as unexpected/abnormal without considering the documented volume/destination change rationale.

actions.label: Apply the transition rationale
actions.exact_action: Use the documented reason to interpret system behavior: during each sort phase, you expect to receive different kind of volume, and you push out that volume before the sort ends.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Sort phases must be cycled because during these sort phases you expect to receive different kind of volume and push out that volume before the sort ends.

steps.title: Check that transitions can still occur during peak season
steps.purpose: To avoid misclassifying peak-season transitions as faults when they are expected by design.
steps.instruction: If you observe transitions even during peak season, confirm the documented expectation that peak season still includes transitions between sort phases.
steps.expected_result: You can explain that even in peak season, transitions between preload/day sort/twilight still occur.
steps.healthy_condition: Your interpretation treats peak-season transitions as consistent with the documented behavior.
steps.failure_condition: You treat peak-season transitions as contradictory to normal operation.

actions.label: Validate peak-season expectation
actions.exact_action: If you observe transitions even during peak season, confirm the documented expectation: peak season still has transitions between sort phases.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Even in peak season, you still have those transitions.

success_criteria: Operator can identify the active conceptual sort phase as preload, day sort, or twilight.
Operator can justify observed transitions using the documented rationale: different volume/destinations by phase require cycling and pushing out volume before the phase ends.
Operator can explain that transitions can still occur during peak season.
healthy_conditions: Operator explanations consistently reference the documented cause: volume goes to different locations across phases, so phases must cycle.
Peak-season transitions are interpreted as expected rather than contradictory.
failure_conditions: Operator assumes phases can run into each other without cycling/clearing.
Operator misclassifies peak-season transitions as abnormal solely due to timing/season.
escalation_guidance: If transitions occur in a way that contradicts the documented need to clear/push out volume before sort end, escalate for support rather than assuming normal behavior.
